purpose: Rules of the 2005 draft lottery (rules only; the real result is never used). The 2004 runtime (runtime/lottery.py) applies the same keys to the simulated league; a 2005 run must take Charlotte into the lottery (no fixed slot) and use 14 lottery clubs.
combinations_status: seeds 4 = 119, 5 = 88 and 6 = 63 and the 17.7% average of seeds 2-3 sourced from contemporaneous 2005 reports (fourth seed 11.9%, fifth seed 8.8%, sixth seed 6.3%, two clubs tied for seeds 2-3 at 17.7% each); seed 1 = 250 and the full 14-club sequence (sum 1,000) derived from Wikipedia's lottery-winner table for 2005-2018 (2005 seed 6 = 63, 2006 seed 5 = 88, 2008 seed 9 = 17, 2011 seed 2 = 199 and seed 8 = 28, 2013 seed 3 = 156) and the 1,000-combination total
ties: Tied clubs split the combinations of the seeds they occupy evenly; an uneven remainder and the order of tied clubs that do not win a top-3 pick are settled by a drawing (sourced for the lottery generally). In the second round tied clubs pick in the opposite order (derived from the 2003 draft).
after_the_lottery: Clubs that do not win a top-3 pick choose in reverse order of record, so no club falls more than three places (derived; no expansion slot in 2005). Charlotte takes part in the lottery like any other non-playoff club (sourced). Playoff clubs follow in reverse order of record (non-lottery ties by drawing); the second round is in reverse order of record of all 30 clubs, unaffected by the lottery (sourced for 2004, same rule).

research.topic: NBA draft lottery rules in force for the 2005 draft lottery (May 24, 2005)
research.scope_note: Rules only. Real 2005 lottery results, real 2004-05 records, real seedings, real tie-break outcomes and real draft order are deliberately omitted (hindsight). Several cited pages also contain those results; the caller must not import them.

event.edition: 21st annual NBA Draft Lottery (derived: the 2004 lottery was the 20th)
sources: https://www.nysun.com/article/sports-sports-desk-2005-05-25 (New York Sun, May 25, 2005: the lottery was held 'Tuesday night in Secaucus, N.J.'; May 24, 2005 was a Tuesday. Page read through a search-engine extract; the site itself returned a bot check)
https://www.ptt.cc/bbs/Bucks/M.1116988481.A.99E.html (message id encodes Unix time 1116988481 = 2005-05-25 02:34 UTC, i.e. the evening of May 24 US Eastern; corroboration only)

participants.rule: All clubs that missed the 2005 playoffs. The league had 30 clubs in 2004-05 (Charlotte's first season) and 16 made the playoffs, so 14 clubs took part.
participants.status: derived (30 clubs minus 16 playoff clubs); 14 combination shares sourced indirectly by the 2005-2018 table

charlotte_expansion.rule: The Charlotte Bobcats' expansion terms fixed their 2004 position only (No. 4). For the 2005 and 2006 drafts Charlotte enters the lottery as an ordinary non-playoff club and is eligible for the No. 1 pick; there is no fixed first- or second-round slot and no cap on how high Charlotte may draw.
charlotte_expansion.quote: The new team will be eligible for the No. 1 pick in the 2005 and 2006 drafts.
sources: https://www.deseret.com/2002/12/21/19695058/draft-rules-favorable-for-charlotte-franchise/ (Deseret News, Dec 21, 2002: fourth pick in 2004; eligible for No. 1 in 2005 and 2006; contrast with Toronto/Vancouver, kept out of the lottery for their first three seasons)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_draft_lottery (1995 Toronto/Vancouver restriction, the precedent that did not apply to Charlotte)
charlotte_expansion.corroboration: Contemporaneous 2005 lottery coverage (search-engine extract) shows Charlotte entering the lottery with a regular seed share, consistent with no special restriction. (Its seed and the other clubs' are real 2004-05 results and are not recorded.)

second_round.rule: No fixed second-round slot in 2005: Charlotte picks in round 2 by its record like every other club.
second_round.note: The 2004 No. 33 slot came from the expansion terms for 2004 only; the Deseret News summary gives no 2005 second-round term, and the 2005 draft table places Charlotte's own second-round pick by record (No. 32). The exact expansion-agreement text is unverified.

mechanics.rule: 14 ping-pong balls numbered 1-14; four drawn; 1,001 combinations regardless of order; 1,000 assigned to the 14 lottery clubs by computer, the one unassigned combination (11-12-13-14) is redrawn. Draw for No. 1, balls returned, repeat for No. 2 and No. 3; a combination belonging to a club that already won a pick is ignored and redrawn.
mechanics.status: sourced (general NBA description); 2005-specific NBA.com How It Works page not retrieved (nba.com feature pages return 'Content Unavailable' and web.archive.org is unreachable from this environment)

seeds_worst_first.note: 250 for the worst record is the 1994-2018 constant (Wikipedia winner table: 2004, 2015-2018 worst seeds 250); 2005 reports name the worst club's chance 'the best' without a figure. Lowest pick = seed + 3.
Wikipedia: 2011 Cleveland, second-worst record, 199 combinations; 2005 report: two clubs tied for seeds 2-3 at 17.7% each = (199 + 156) / 2 rounded.
2005 report: fifth seed 8.8%; Wikipedia: 2006 Toronto, fifth-worst, 88.
2005 report: sixth seed 6.3%; Wikipedia winner table: 2005, sixth-worst, 63 (out of 1,000).
14-club 2005-2018 sequence (remainder of the 1,000 after the sourced and Wikipedia-confirmed seeds is 11 + 8 + 7 + 6 + 5 = 37).
Best lottery club keeps the 5 combinations it had in the 13-club table (nba_2004_lottery_rules.json).

combination_table_14_clubs.derivation: The 13-club 1995-2004 table (250-200-157-120-89-64-44-29-18-11-7-6-5) became the 14-club table 250-199-156-119-88-63-43-28-17-11-8-7-6-5 when the league reached 30 clubs; the 2005 brief in nba_2004_lottery_rules.json (correction_to_brief) already names this as the table used from 2005 to 2018. The values for seeds 4-6 match the 2005 reports exactly, the 2-3 tie average matches 17.7%, and the sum is 1,000.
sources: https://hoopsrumors.com/2016/08/poll-2005-nba-draft-take-two-pick-no-14.html and contemporaneous 2005 coverage surfaced by search (17.7% tied seeds 2-3, 11.9%, 8.8%, 6.3% for seeds 4-6); the 2005 NBA.com odds page itself could not be retrieved
combination_table_14_clubs.chances_no2_no3: NBA.com also publishes No. 2/No. 3 chances per club; these follow from the drawing procedure (sequential draw without the previous winners) and can be computed from the combination counts.

ties.rule: Clubs with identical records split the combinations of the seeds they occupy equally (average). If the average is not an integer, a random drawing decides which club gets the extra combination. That same drawing decides which tied club picks earlier if neither wins a top-3 pick, and the order of the tied clubs is reversed in the second round.
ties.status: sourced (averaging and drawing, general rule); derived (second-round reversal)
ties.timing: Ties were broken by random drawing shortly after the regular season, before the lottery (2004: April 15; the 2005 drawing date is unverified).
ties.second_round_reversal_evidence: Same evidence as nba_2004_lottery_rules.json: in the 2003 draft two clubs tied at 37-45 picked 9th and 10th in round 1 and in the opposite order in round 2 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_NBA_draft). No 2005-specific rule text found: status derived. (The 2005 draft table shows the same reversal for a tied pair; that real outcome is deliberately not recorded.)

no_drop_more_than.rule: Clubs not winning a top-3 pick select in inverse order of regular-season record after the three winners, so no club falls more than three places: seed k picks no lower than min(k + 3, 14).
no_drop_more_than.status: derived (three drawn picks, no fixed expansion slot in 2005)

non_lottery_and_second_round.first_round_15_on: Playoff clubs pick after the lottery in inverse order of regular-season record (playoff results do not matter), ties by random drawing. In 2005 these were picks 15-30: the first round had 30 selections (no forfeited pick).
non_lottery_and_second_round.first_round_status: sourced (30 first-round picks, Wikipedia/BBR 2005 draft tables); derived (no forfeit: Minnesota made its own 2005 first-round selection, so its 2000 salary-cap sanction did not reach 2005)
non_lottery_and_second_round.second_round: All 30 clubs pick in inverse order of regular-season record; the lottery does not affect round 2. Tied clubs reverse their round-1 order.
non_lottery_and_second_round.second_round_status: sourced (inverse record, lottery not applied: NBC Sports/NBA explainer); derived (tie reversal)

traded_picks.rule: A traded lottery pick keeps the original club's seed and combinations; a non-playoff club holding another lottery club's pick gets both seeds' combinations. Protected picks stay with the original club when the drawn or record slot falls inside the protection (nba_2005_pick_ownership.json).

larry_coon_cbafaq.note: Coon's 2005-CBA Salary Cap FAQ (www.cbafaq.com/salarycap05.htm) covers draft-pick trading but not lottery odds, tie-breaks or draft order; the lottery is governed by the NBA (Board of Governors), not the CBA. Nothing taken from it.

research.hindsight_warning: The New York Sun report, Wikipedia's 2005 NBA draft and lottery pages, the Hoops Rumors poll and the search extracts contain the real 2004-05 records, seedings and lottery winners. None of those results is recorded here; the club percentages were used only to confirm seed combination counts.
